cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A query plan is the strategy the optimizer picks to run a SQL statement: index or full scan, join order and join algorithm, based on table statistics. EXPLAIN shows it; EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs the query and adds real timings and row counts.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Look for sequential scans on big tables, bad row estimates and expensive joins. Fix with the right index, a rewritten query, updated statistics, or removing N+1 queries. Composite index order matters: it serves the leading columns. Always measure before and after.

questions.q: You added an index but still see a Seq Scan. Is it broken?
questions.a: Usually not. If the condition matches a large share of rows a scan is cheaper, or statistics are stale.

questions.q: What is the N+1 query problem?
questions.a: One query per row of an earlier result, like 50 orders then 50 item queries. Fix with a join, WHERE id IN, or eager loading.
EXPLAIN shows estimated plan and cost; EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs it with real timings and row counts.
